sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Automotive Replacement Parts and Tuning Accessories

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Colombia (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (unitary national system; Spanish-heritage commercial law codified in Código de Comercio with the S.A.S. special regime governed by Law 1258 of 2008)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: AML/CFT: Law 526 of 1999 (UIAF), Law 1121 of 2006, Law 1621 of 2013, Decree 1674 of 2016, Circular Básica Jurídica 100-000005 of 2021 (Superintendencia de Sociedades) and Circular Externa 009 of 2016. UBO: Decree 830 of 2021, Law 2184 of 2022, and Resolution DIAN 164 of 2023 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales). Statutory UBO registration threshold is 5% of capital, voting rights, or control (Resolution 164 of 2023, Art. 4); for enhanced due diligence escalation, an internal 25% benchmark is applied as a secondary red-flag trigger.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (UBO filings before DIAN and the Cámara de Comercio are confidential, not publicly searchable; available only to DIAN, UIAF, Superintendencia de Sociedades, and judicial authorities)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation granted by foreign shareholders and directors
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia acceded through Law 455 of 1998, in force since 2001) plus certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport copy and proof of residential address of each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign government authority or notary in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry or competent registrar of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille plus certified Spanish translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for each UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization followed by Hague Apostille; for non-Hague Convention states, consular legalization at the Colombian embassy or consulate

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, UBOs, and legal representatives against the OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, UIAF Lista de Riesgo and Listas de Personas Expuestas Políticamente, and the Superintendencia de Sociedades sanctions register. Screening must be documented at onboarding and refreshed at least quarterly; any PEP status requires enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and compliance-officer sign-off under Circular Básica Jurídica 100-000005 of 2021.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial (www.rues.org.co); formal name-reservation request filed before the Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered office (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered business name must be in Spanish or use Spanish-compatible characters; foreign-language names must be transliterated phonetically into the Spanish alphabet and may not contain symbols or exclusively non-Latin script. The name must satisfy the legal dissimilarity doctrine and be clearly distinguishable from existing names in the RUES database.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Any term suggesting financial, securities, or regulated activities
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon administrative rejection, the applicant may (1) file a recurso de reposición before the same Cámara de Comercio within ten (10) business days of notification, and (2) alternatively lodge a recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio within the same ten (10) business days. If the reservation lapses without registration, a new homonymy certificate and reapplication are required at the applicable tariff.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Partially permissible – the S.A.S. bylaws must designate a physical domicile in Colombian territory for service of process (Art. 18, Law 1258 of 2008). Registered virtual offices in Bogotá, Medellín, and Cali are accepted provided they include a physical address, documented acceptance by the provider, and mail-forwarding services; a P.O. Box alone or a purely digital address is not acceptable.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-to-low (estimated 25–35% annual probability). DIAN and Cámaras de Comercio may conduct unannounced inspections of the registered establishment (establecimiento de comercio) to verify RUT, accounting records, and operational continuity. The auto-parts e-commerce model is classified as Low_Risk_Standard, so inspections are expected to be documentary unless discrepancies are flagged.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Homonymy certificate (certificado de homonimia) for S.A.S. name reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff set by Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (approx. COP 23,000)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of private incorporation document (minuta S.A.S.)
Hague Apostille of three foreign documents (POA, passport, certificate of good standing)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs / competent authority of the state of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of USD 50 per apostilled document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign apostilled documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market rate of USD 30–50 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration rights and derechos de inscripción (S.A.S. entry in the commercial registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff on declared capital (approx. COP 300,000 for minimum-level capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration tax (impuesto de registro) on incorporation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Municipal/district treasury (e.g., Secretaría de Hacienda de Bogotá)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: 0.7% of declared capital for non-real-estate acts per Decree-Law 1250 of 1970, calculated on COP 50,000,000 declared capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sarlaft (AML) manual, PEP screening protocol, and UBO file design
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for low-risk e-commerce entities: fixed fee USD 600–750

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate legal counsel for bylaw drafting, post-incorporation registry filings, and foreign-shareholder structuring
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee for S.A.S. incorporation with foreign UBOs: USD 800–1,200

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law 1258 of 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada, Arts. 1-54) as amended by Law 1450 of 2011; Colombian Commercial Code (Decree 410 of 1971), Arts. 110 and 372-386; Decree 1074 of 2015 (Sole Regulatory Decree on Commerce) on mercantile registration (Registro Mercantil); Law 1480 of 2011 (consumer protection) for e-commerce operations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial competence over the registered office, operating through the Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online portal
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation instrument) executed by all founding shareholders, inscribed in the Registro Mercantil (mercantile registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum subscribed or paid-in capital is required under Law 1258 of 2008; the capital is freely determined in the bylaws and may be paid in cash or in kind, with payment deferred up to two (2) years; no escrow account obligation attaches to S.A.S. incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION NO. 001 OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. — The undersigned founding shareholders, acting as the supreme corporate body, RESOLVE: FIRST: To ratify the subscription and payment of the corporate capital in the proportions stated in the incorporation instrument. SECOND: To adopt as the registered office the address filed with the Chamber of Commerce: [Calle 00 No. 00-00], Bogotá D.C., Colombia. THIRD: To appoint [Shareholder A] as Legal Representative and [Shareholder B] as Deputy Legal Representative with the powers granted by Law 1258 of 2008 and the bylaws. FOURTH: To authorize the Legal Representative to effect all filings, DIAN tax enrollment, social security registrations and bank account openings necessary to complete the Company's legal operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio — Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) online portal or service window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name availability search (consulta de homonimia) and reserve the proposed corporate denomination for thirty (30) calendar days; obtain the Certificado de Homonimia confirming that no identical or confusingly similar prior registration exists in the same Chamber of Commerce jurisdiction.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name with up to three alternatives
Identification numbers of all founding shareholders
Completed RUES name reservation request form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name conflicts with an existing registration, submit an alternative denomination from the proposed list; the reservation may be renewed once for an additional thirty (30) days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the private incorporation instrument
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding shareholders, with optional authentication before a Colombian Notaría
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the Documento Privado de Constitución stating: shareholder identification; corporate name ending in S.A.S.; domicile; corporate purpose covering online retail of automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories (ISIC 4791); capital subscription and payment terms; administration and legal representation rules; fiscal year. Signatures must bear fingerprints and be authenticated when any shareholder is a foreign non-resident or when real estate is contributed to the capital.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Homonimia
Valid passports or national IDs of all founding shareholders
Drafted bylaws of the S.A.S.
Notarized power of attorney for each shareholder acting through a representative
Bank or notarial authentication of signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If formal defects are later identified by the Chamber of Commerce, execute a corrective amendment (reforma) or re-execute the instrument with a revised signature page, preserving the priority of the original filing date for name-reservation purposes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile registration with the Chamber of Commerce (RUES)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio with territorial competence over the registered office, via RUES digital platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed incorporation instrument with the Chamber of Commerce, pay the registration administrative fee and the registro tax (impuesto de registro, generally 0.7% of subscribed capital), and obtain the Matrícula Mercantil (merchant registration). The Chamber automatically transmits registration data to DIAN, which assigns the provisional NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria).
required_dossiers: Signed Documento Privado de Constitución
Shareholder identification documents
Certificado de Homonimia
Acceptance letter of the Legal Representative
Preliminary RUT form data sheet for DIAN transmission
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber raises observations (falencias), cure the marked defects within the statutory correction window (typically five (5) days) by filing corrected pages; minor omissions are corrected without loss of the filing priority.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Definitive tax enrollment at DIAN (RUT and NIT confirmation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — MUISCA online portal or local office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the definitive RUT (Registro Único Tributario) using the provisional NIT, confirm the ordinary corporate income tax regime, set the economic activity code for ISIC 4791, select the invoicing group, and enable electronic invoicing (factura electrónica) pursuant to Resolution 000165 of 2023.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal issued by the Chamber of Commerce
Legal Representative identification document
Proof of registered-office address
Provisional NIT assigned at mercantile registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN rejects or queries the enrollment for missing data, correct the RUT fields through the MUISCA system, revalidate the supporting documents, and resubmit the enrollment request without additional registry fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security enrollment, ARL contracting and corporate bank account opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Pension fund administrator (AFP), EPS, occupational risk insurer (ARL), Caja de Compensación Familiar, and commercial banking institution
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Affiliate the Legal Representative and any employees to the social security system under Law 100 of 1993, contract an ARL occupational risk policy before hiring the first employee, register the employer with a Caja de Compensación Familiar, and open a corporate current account presenting the Chamber certificate of existence and legal representation issued within the last 90 days; configure the bank account for Stripe and PayPal payouts under the company's legal name.
required_dossiers: NIT and definitive RUT
Certificate of Existence and Legal Representation (90 days validity)
Shareholder resolution appointing the Legal Representative
Legal Representative identification document
Corporate bank account application form with beneficial-ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or administrator raises a query, obtain an updated certificate of existence, align the bylaws and certificate data, and resubmit the application; for ARL discrepancies, coordinate with the insurer to issue a corrected enrollment certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal ICA registration, fire safety certification and e-commerce compliance registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda (Bogotá) or municipal treasury; Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos; Curaduría Urbana; Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company in the municipal ICA (Impuesto de Industria y Comercio) padron for online retail activity; obtain the annual Certificado de Bomberos for the registered office or warehouse; secure the zoning/occupancy certificate (Licencia de Uso de Suelo) where a physical premises exists; and register the e-commerce personal databases with the SIC Registro de Bases de Datos under Law 1581 of 2012.
required_dossiers: RUT and NIT certificates
Current Chamber of Commerce certificate
Lease agreement or property title of the registered office and warehouse
Floor plan and fire-safety equipment list for the fire department inspection
Privacy policy and data-processing notice for the SIC database registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ICA padron or fire certificate is queried, present the corrected registered-address certificate, adjust occupancy and capacity data, and schedule a re-inspection by the fire department; if the SIC requests clarifications, file a corrective amendment to the database registration application.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No industrial manufacturing license applies; e-commerce retail under ISIC 4791 is governed by the Chamber of Commerce registries (RUES/Matrícula Mercantil) and, where a physical warehouse or office is established, by the municipal zoning and occupancy permit (Licencia de Uso de Suelo) granted by the Curaduría Urbana or local planning authority.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable — the activity does not require a statutory operating license; the company must maintain a valid Matrícula Mercantil and municipal ICA registration. Online sales must comply with Law 1480 of 2011 (consumer protection) and the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio disclosure rules for e-commerce merchants, while Stripe and PayPal integration requires the RUT, NIT and a Colombian corporate bank account.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA) for national-level projects; for minor commercial premises, the Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) or the competent municipal environmental authority
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from full EIA — retail, warehousing and distribution of automotive replacement parts is a low-impact activity requiring only a simplified environmental registration (Ficha Ambiental) or an express exemption certificate from the competent environmental authority; no full EIA report or environmental license is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Any non-domestic wastewater discharges must comply with Resolution 0631 of 2015 (pH 6.0–9.0; BOD5 ≤ 250 mg/L; TSS ≤ 250 mg/L; oils and greases ≤ 20 mg/L). Hazardous wastes (used batteries, oils, lubricants, coolant fluids) must be managed under the reverse-logistics regime of Resolution 1257 of 2021 using certified waste carriers. VOC and particulate emissions from sealed-part storage are negligible and do not require an atmospheric discharge permit where stock quantities remain below the thresholds of Decree 1076 of 2015.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate (Certificado de Bomberos) issued annually by the Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos covering the warehouse or business premises; structural and seismic compliance with NSR-10 (Reglamento Colombiano de Construcción Sismo Resistente); Sistema de Gestión de Seguridad y Salud en el Trabajo (SG-SST) implemented and registered with the chosen ARL pursuant to Resolution 0312 of 2019; occupational risk insurance (ARL) contracted before the first employee is hired; accessibility compliance per Law 1618 of 2013 for any open-to-public premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN); electronic portal MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) at www.dian.gov.co.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned S.A.S.: file the RUT (Registro Único Tributario) with DIAN through MUISCA before taxable operations; the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) is assigned upon approval. Non-resident shareholders must apostille constitution and power-of-attorney documents; the resident legal representative activates fiscal credentials and e-invoicing certification. A non-resident entity without a Colombian permanent establishment may also obtain a NIT through a resident attorney-in-fact.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — resident S.A.S. taxed on worldwide income at the standard 35% corporate rate (2025); non-resident shareholders and payment processors are taxed only on Colombian-source income via withholding; no pass-through or territorial-election relief available to the S.A.S.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election in Colombia. Optional mechanisms: (i) consolidated income-tax filing for domestic subgroups (Articles 43-46 E.T.); (ii) the 3% remittance tax on gross payments abroad for technical/administrative services where the non-resident beneficiary has no PE (Article 406 E.T.), elected instead of a full Colombian return; (iii) DIAN-published transfer-pricing safe harbors. Hybrid-mismatch rules (Law 2010/2019, Article 56) are mandatory and non-elective.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia) and the Comisión de Cambios, with supervisory enforcement by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia and the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) for exchange declaration purposes.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Capital account and current account transactions are generally convertible under the framework of Ley 9 de 1991, the Régimen de Cambios Internacionales, and Circular Reglamentaria DCIN 83 of 2018 of the Banco de la República (compiled in the new External Exchange Manual). Legal profit remittances by foreign direct investors in Colombian S.A.S. entities are permitted without prior exchange authorization provided the investment is duly registered with the Banco de la República, the remittance is made through authorized foreign exchange intermediaries or local banks using the appropriate declaration codes, applicable taxes (e.g., dividend withholding tax and CREE-related levies) are evidenced, and the 11% remittance tax on branch profits (impuesto de remesas) is not applicable to dividends paid out of taxed profits of an S.A.S. (only to the net income of permanent establishments that are not branches of a foreign entity; for branches, the 33% remittance tax applies on remitted profits net of tax). Foreign exchange market participation in Colombia is compulsory for most cross-border payments and receipts, meaning payments must be channeled through the foreign exchange market (canal de la cuenta corriente) with the corresponding market participant, unless the transaction falls within a listed exception. The Colombian peso is convertible under a managed floating exchange rate regime. Restrictions apply to non-financial private sector borrowing and certain capital flows; all foreign credit, portfolio investment, and direct investment must be declared to the central bank. For the sale of automotive parts via e-commerce to foreign customers, export of services and goods export proceeds must be surrendered and settled through the Colombian foreign exchange market within specified timelines, and retained foreign currency must be declared. Settlement delays can be authorized only under specific circumstances (e.g., temporary import/export, advance payments, guarantees, or accounts abroad previously authorized by the central bank). Dividends to non-resident shareholders are freely transferable once registered, but the remittance must be processed through an authorized intermediary with an exchange declaration and the exporting company must evidence that the relevant tax obligations have been fulfilled.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Colombian foreign exchange regime, proceeds from exports of goods (including online retail sales of automotive parts where the goods physically leave Colombia) must be channeled through the foreign exchange market. General rule: export proceeds must be received through the foreign exchange market within 6 months from the date of shipment or from the filing of the export declaration, unless the exporter has obtained an extension from the Banco de la República under Circular Reglamentaria DCIN 83. Of those proceeds, 100% must be surrendered/settled by converting into Colombian pesos if the proceeds are received in a foreign currency, except for the portion that the exporter wishes to maintain in foreign currency under an authorized foreign currency account (cuenta de compensación or cuenta en el exterior) previously declared to the central bank; however, even in that case the surrender requirement is not a fractional partial conversion but an obligation to bring all proceeds into the Colombian foreign exchange market within the legal term. Funds may be received directly in COP in the exporter's local account if the foreign buyer pays via a wire transfer in COP, although such COP transfers from offshore are subject to exchange control and must be declared as a service or goods export under the corresponding declaration code. Specific statutory timeline: The 6-month period is applied from the date of the export declaration (Declaración de Exportación – DEX) or the date of shipment for goods, and from the date of accrual/invoice issue for services. Non-compliance triggers a fine under the regulatory enforcement powers of DIAN and the Banco de la República, plus late surrender interest obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente in COP) for e-commerce receipts and trade operating expenses; a separate Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Inversión Extranjera) is held with the same bank for inbound FDI registration
Operational Account for trade settlements and payroll; foreign direct investment capital escrow account where required
Operational Account for merchant acquiring and treasury sweep accounts
Operational Account and FX hedging collateral account
Operational Account for trade finance and letters of credit operations; capital account if regional treasury concentration desired

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Itaú Corpbanca Colombia (now Banco Itaú Colombia S.A.)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account for cross-border wire receipts and cash management
Operational Account for retail card settlement and low-risk e-commerce volume

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium-Low for principal treasury rails and High only as a supplementary fringe route. Legal constraints: (i) Non-bank fintech companies in Colombia are not authorized by the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia to offer deposit-taking, current account, or cross-border payment services unless licensed as a Sociedad Especializada en Pagos (SEDPE) or as a financial institution; foreign Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) without a local license may not provide regulated payment services to Colombian residents. (ii) Foreign EMIs such as Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex cannot substitute for a Colombian domestic bank account for the surrender of export proceeds, because the Colombian exchange regime requires all export-related foreign currency to be returned to Colombia through the foreign exchange market and to be declared through a local authorized intermediary or through the simple export declaration process where no local financial intermediary is involved if the funds remain abroad in an authorized foreign currency account. (iii) For an S.A.S. with Colombian e-commerce operations, inbound buyer payments from abroad via PayPal and Stripe are generally paid out to a local bank in COP; if the company maintains a foreign currency account with a foreign EMI, that account must be declared as a cuenta en el exterior to the Banco de la República, and the funds must be repatriated within the 6-month surrender window unless a specific exchange authorization is obtained. (iv) The target payment rails (Stripe and PayPal) are viable as acquiring subprocessors that settle in COP or USD through local bank partners, but legal clearance must be handled by a Colombian-licensed commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a Colombian S.A.S., but a fully remote opening is feasible under certain conditions. Under the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia's KYC rules and circular norms on remote customer onboarding (e.g., Circular Externa 029 de 2014 and the simplified remote onboarding provisions enacted for digital onboarding), banks may permit remote account opening for non-face-to-face customers after applying enhanced due diligence, including a video call interview, digital identity verification via the Registraduría (authentic citizen ID), and electronic signatures (firma electrónica). In practice, tier-1 Colombian banks (Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, Davivienda) require at least one legal representative or a designated company officer with a Colombian RUT and passport/cédula to complete a notarized power of attorney or appear for a video interview; for foreign directors without local presence, most banks individually assess the AML risk. A physical presence mandate is not codified in Colombian law, but banks treat it as an internal policy measure. The best defense is: (i) have at least one statutory representative (representante legal) resident in Colombia or with a Colombian appointed attorney-in-fact; (ii) use a Colombian certified public accountant (revisor fiscal) for the annual audit; and (iii) execute the opening with corporate documents apostilled, legalized under Colombian law, and translated into Spanish.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: S.A.S. with 100% foreign shareholders and no Colombian resident legal representative
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized power of attorney appointing a Colombian attorney-in-fact; apostilled certificate of incorporation and by-laws; shareholder registry and ultimate beneficial owner declaration (UBO); Colombian RUT for the entity; passports of all shareholders; corporate banking questionnaire; lease agreement or registered registered address in Colombia; reference letters from the home-bank for each shareholder; sworn statement of source of funds for the US$0-15,000,000 contribution (if below minimum thresholds, still requested); Colombian criminal background certificates for any resident representative.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce business selling automotive parts online, with disproportionate cross-border e-commerce chargebacks or a high volume of small-value inbound wires from foreign countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed e-commerce merchant record: domain registration, platform agreements (PayPal/Stripe), marketplace sales history, logistics contracts with cross-border couriers (e.g., DHL/FedEx) and customs brokers; export declarations and shipping bills of lading for a representative 12-month period; supplier and purchaser invoices; product catalog and trademark registration; certified financial statements translated to Spanish; AML compliance manual for the company with risk scoring maps for customers; confirmation from the e-commerce platform of seller verification (KYC) in force.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of Stripe and PayPal as primary receivables rails without a Colombian-licensed acquiring partner and with flows held offshore
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written opinion of local AML counsel that the flows qualify as export proceeds; registrations/declarations before Banco de la República for any foreign currency account (cuenta de compensación/cuenta en el exterior) if the company elects to hold settlement funds offshore; evidence of the 6-month repatriation plan (bank statements showing conversion of USD to COP in the local account), and a legal compliance manual establishing the obligation to declare all cross-border receipts to DIAN.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SAS capital under the statutory minimum of an SME or zero-issued shares, raising a suspicious contradiction with declared business volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarial and registration documents of the SAS under Ley 1258 de 2008, with the share subscription agreement and time schedule for payment; an independent accountant's certified statement that no statutory minimum capital is required and that the corporate commercial registry (cámara de comercio) certification evidences the registered paid-in capital in line with the business scale; a plan and shareholder commitment letter to capitalize via a bank transfer subject to exchange control declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Directors or UBOs residing in jurisdictions classified as risky by FATF/GAFILAT or in jurisdictions with no tax information exchange with Colombia
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Source-of-wealth report prepared by a Colombian-licensed attorney; passport and residence card; tax residency certificate issued by the home-country tax authority; official registry entry (RUT) showing Colombian tax ID; list of all companies and affiliations; evidence of economic substance in Colombia (physical office in Bogotá/Medellín, payroll, utility bills); sworn declaration under Article 2.14.1.3 of the Superintendencia's UBO rule with documentary appendix.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border international trade settlement patterns where funds are received from a foreign buyer but the shipping route is Colombia-to-third-country (triangulation)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Commercial agreement shipped, bill of lading with Incoterms, customs transit declarations, DIAN export declaration for the triangulated trade, exchange declaration code for transit trade, Acuerdo de Reintegro if the seller is a mere intermediary; evidence of prior authorization if a foreign currency account is used.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Colombian S.A.S., inbound capital injections from a foreign shareholder must be routed through a Colombian authorized foreign exchange intermediary (e.g., Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, Davivienda) using SWIFT MT103/MT202, with the payment reason encoded as foreign direct investment (FDI). The transfer must be coded as Concept 3610 (Importación de capital para inversión directa de capital) or Concept 3620/3640 depending on the capital type; the receiving bank must file the Declaración de Cambio – Inversión Internacional (Formulario 3) with the Banco de la República within the same business day or by the next business day. The company must obtain a Registro de Inversiones Internacionales (the 'Formulario No. 3' registration) within 2 months from the date of receipt if the capital exceeds US$100,000; if below that threshold, the registration may be simplified or waived. The capital injection must be evidenced by: (i) a corporate resolution approving the capital increase and share subscription; (ii) the legalization of the capital increase before the Cámara de Comercio; (iii) the receipt through a registered local bank account; (iv) certified translation of the resolution into Spanish. After registration, the FDI capital has right to free repatriation and dividend remittance subject to tax and exchange declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade payments for the purchase of automotive aftermarket parts (e.g., from US, China, Germany, Japan) must be routed through the Colombian foreign exchange market. Standard clearing rails: (i) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire payments to the foreign supplier; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) issued by a local bank via SWIFT MT700/MT707 with the corresponding documents (AWBs, shipping invoices, certificates of origin, inspection certificates); (iii) documentary collections (CAD) via MT400/MT798. All payments must be declared to the Banco de la República under the appropriate exchange declaration code (import of goods, concept 3010 or similar) within the month following the transaction or upon the 'momento de declaración' according to Circular DCIN 83. The allocations must include proper importer registration (RUT), previous import declaration, valid inscription in the Registry of Importers/Exporters of DIAN, and retention of the formed MIC/DTA (Declaración de importación anticipada) if applicable. For payments to related companies, beware of the adjusted transfer-pricing documentation rules under Colombian tax law and the thin-capitalization rules.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – COP/USD non-deliverable forwards with local banks or international counterparties satisfying the Superintendencia Financiera marks and eligible through the forward market (Mercado de Derivados Cambiarios)
Currency forwards (deliverable) on the Colombian Peso executed with authorized intermediaries and recorded in the exchange declarations (Formulario 4 for derivative transactions)
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) entered into by qualified counterparties for management of long-term debt and investments
Plain-vanilla and financially settled currency options (calls and puts) on USD/COP with a Colombian authorized financial institution
FX swaps (swap cambiario) with bank counterparties, including the Banco de la República's standing facilities for market makers

Exchange-traded futures on TRM (the Colombian indicative exchange rate) traded through licensed local futures-clearing members (Cámara de Riesgo Central de Contraparte) – limited to hedging actual commercial exposures

Forwards on a basket of currencies or on foreign currency (USD/EUR/CNY) as OTC derivatives with local banks subject to the Superintendencia's derivative registration rules and the ban on speculative positions without real commercial exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal and National Franchise Registry Fee (Renovacion de la Matricula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Camara de Comercio of the registered office jurisdiction in the Confecamaras network
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 March for the preceding year; renewal window runs from 1 January to 31 March, subject to occasional ministry decree extensions
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal surcharge of approximately USD 5-18 per the Chamber of Commerce graduated tariff; failure to renew by year-end leads to cancellation of the mercantile registration, and the S.A.S. risks administrative strike-off and loss of corporate legal standing (personalidad juridica) as well as restrictions on contracting with financial institutions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return and Complementary Tax Declaration (Declaracion de Renta y Complementario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Direccion de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by the DIAN-published deadline for the preceding fiscal year ending 31 December, generally in August of the following calendar year, phased by the last two digits of the corporate NIT tax ID
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing surcharge (sancion por extemporaneidad) of up to 5% of the income tax payable, or a minimum fine of approximately USD 135 where no tax is payable, plus monthly default interest on unpaid corporate income tax; DIAN enforcement and collection proceedings begin immediately after the filing deadline.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner Confirmation Report (Reporte Anual de Beneficiario Final via SIRUBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Camara de Comercio through the Superintendencia de Sociedades SIRUBO system, with data shared with DIAN and UIAF
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 30 July covering the preceding calendar year; every shareholding transfer occurring during the year must be updated within 30 days of the transfer and reflected in the annual confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing, late filing, or material misstatement is punishable under Colombian anti-money-laundering regulations (Law 526 of 1999, as amended) with fines up to approximately USD 2,000; in practice it also blocks issuance of valid commercial registry certificates and KYC/AML approvals required by payment rails such as Stripe and PayPal.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary Shareholders Meeting and Approval of Statutory Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Internal corporate governance record maintained in the corporate minute books; no regulatory filing is required unless a capital or bylaw amendment occurs, in which case the minutes are filed with the Chamber of Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be convened and held at least once per year within three calendar months after the 31 December fiscal year-end, i.e., by 31 March of each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omission triggers potential administrative fines from the Superintendencia de Sociedades; the company may be deemed to be operating irregularly under Article 142 of the Código de Comercio and may face formal intervention; unapproved financial statements cannot lawfully support dividend distributions or capital reductions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Exogenous Tax Information Report (Informacion Exogena filed through SIIT/SOH)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually per the DIAN resolution in force, generally between June and August of the year following the taxable calendar year, phased by the last two digits of the NIT; mandatory where the S.A.S. has payment obligations, withholdings, or third-party transactions above the statutory threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or inaccurate filing exposes the company to the Article 651 Estatuto Tributario sanction of up to 5% of the values subject to reporting, subject to statutory minimum fines of approximately USD 130, plus daily delay charges where the report reveals omitted withholding taxes.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A S.A.S. must appoint a compulsory independent statutory auditor (revisor fiscal) when, at the prior 31 December, it exceeds any of: (i) gross assets of 5,000 statutory minimum monthly wages (SMMLV), approximately COP 6,500,000,000 or USD 1,560,000 on the 2024 wage base of COP 1,300,000; (ii) gross ordinary revenues of 3,000 SMMLV, approximately COP 3,900,000,000 or USD 940,000; or (iii) more than 30 employees. Below these thresholds audited financial statements are not compulsory unless required by the bylaws, investor agreements, or payment-rail contracts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (NIIF) as adopted in Colombia under Law 1314 of 2009; the auto-parts e-commerce S.A.S. is classified in Group 2 and applies NIIF para las PYMES (IFRS for SMEs); financial statements are expressed in Colombian pesos, approved by the annual shareholders meeting, and filed with the Superintendencia de Sociedades only where the statutory size thresholds apply.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual protocol: by 30 July of each calendar year the S.A.S. must file or reconfirm its Beneficiary Final Owner schedule through the Chamber of Commerce SIRUBO portal, identifying every ultimate natural person holding directly or indirectly 10% or more of the share capital, voting rights, profits, or control. Any share transfer taking place during the year must be updated within 30 days of the transfer and cross-checked against the Shareholder Registry Book before the annual confirmation. The same UBO dataset must be refreshed for AML/KYC reviews of the Stripe and PayPal payment rails.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Registro de Asamblea y Juntas Directivas)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas y Decisiones Sociales)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 150-600 per year for registered office and registered agent services covering legal notifications and coordination of the annual commercial registry renewal and UBO filings in the Colombian Chamber of Commerce network
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800-2,500 per year for a certified Colombian public accountant performing the statutory review or SME IFRS audit, depending on transaction volume and register size
